description: Add history of appendectomy at age 22
presentation: A 50-year-old man with IgA nephropathy, diabetes insipidus, recurrent UTIs, and a history of appendectomy at age 22 presents with suspected drug allergy after Bactrim for UTI: pruritus and hives on arms/trunk began after the 4th dose; patient self-discontinued after the following dose. He also noted dark urine, and labs showed AKI (Cr 2.5 from baseline 1.2) that resolved over the next month. He previously tolerated once-daily low-dose Bactrim for 6 months 10 years ago. Does the patient need sulfa allergy testing? Is the AKI was part of an allergic reaction or a separate adverse effect?
